content: When using this medication, you may initially notice a worsening of your symptoms. This is a common occurrence when starting praziquantel. Side Effects: Common side effects include headache, dizziness, stomach pain, nausea, fatigue, weakness, joint or muscle pain, loss of appetite, vomiting, and sweating. These effects are typically mild and temporary. They may also be related to your underlying parasitic infection or the process of the parasites dying off. It is important to remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits to your health outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the U.S. or Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding any side effects you experience. Precautions: Before taking praziquantel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness during treatment and up to the day after treatment. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Praziquantel can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect how praziquantel is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole), chloroquine, cimetidine, dexamethasone, efavirenz, macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), and rifamycins (e.g., rifampin). Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring: While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., urine or stool examination, biopsy of infected tissue) should be conducted to monitor your condition. If you have a heart condition, additional monitoring may be required. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
